title: Perform basic life support and first aid procedures

lessons.title: Emergency scene and the body
lessons.html:
Important

This lesson helps you understand first aid. It does not replace hands-on training. You must complete practical training with an accredited first aid provider before you act as a first aider.

Managing the emergency scene

When someone is hurt, first make sure you are safe. A dead or injured first aider cannot help anyone.

  1. Danger: look for dangers: a running tractor, electricity, fire, chemicals, an angry bull, traffic. Make it safe: switch off engines, stop people coming close. If you cannot make it safe, do not go in; call for help.
  2. Protect yourself from blood and body fluids: wear gloves from the first aid box.
  3. Call for help: shout for others, and phone emergency services. In South Africa, 10177 is the national ambulance number, and 112 works from a cell phone. Know your farm's emergency numbers and the farm's address or GPS location to give the ambulance.
  4. Keep others back and give the injured person space.

Basic parts of the body

SystemWhat it does
Airway and lungsTake air in and out. The airway goes from the mouth and nose to the lungs.
Heart and blood vesselsThe heart pumps blood with oxygen around the body.
Brain and nervesControl the body. The brain is damaged within minutes without oxygen.
Bones and musclesSupport and move the body. The spine protects the spinal cord.
SkinProtects the body from germs, heat and cold.

This is why breathing and blood flow come first in first aid: without oxygen reaching the brain, a person can die in minutes.

lessons.title: Assessing the person and life support
lessons.html:
Check the person

Use DRSABC:

  • Danger: is the area safe?
  • Response: tap the shoulders and ask loudly, "Are you all right?"
  • Send for help: call the ambulance, or ask someone to call and bring the first aid kit (and an AED if there is one).
  • Airway: if there is no response, gently tilt the head back and lift the chin to open the airway.
  • Breathing: look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
  • CPR: if the person is not breathing normally, start CPR.

CPR for an adult

  1. Kneel next to the person on a firm surface.
  2. Put the heel of one hand in the centre of the chest, other hand on top.
  3. Keep your arms straight and press down hard and fast, about 5 to 6 cm deep, 100 to 120 times a minute. Let the chest come back up after each push.
  4. If trained and willing, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 compressions. If not, do compressions only without stopping.
  5. If an AED arrives, switch it on and follow its voice instructions.
  6. Continue until help takes over, the person starts breathing normally, or you are too exhausted to go on.

Unconscious but breathing

Put the person in the recovery position (on their side, head tilted back so the airway stays open). Keep checking breathing. If you suspect a spine injury, for example after a fall from a trailer, keep the head and neck still and move them only if the airway is at risk or the scene is dangerous.

Choking

If an adult is choking and cannot cough or speak: give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts. Repeat. If they become unconscious, start CPR and call for help.

lessons.title: Treating bleeding and common injuries
lessons.html:
Severe bleeding

  1. Wear gloves.
  2. Press firmly on the wound with a clean dressing or cloth.
  3. Keep pressing. If blood soaks through, put another dressing on top; do not remove the first.
  4. Bandage firmly over the dressing.
  5. Lay the person down and keep them warm. Watch for shock: pale, cold, sweaty skin and a fast pulse. Get help fast.

Common farm injuries

InjuryFirst aid
Small cuts and grazesClean with clean water, cover with a plaster or dressing
BurnsCool under cool running water for at least 20 minutes. Do not use butter, toothpaste or ice. Cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy cloth. Get medical help for large burns.
Chemical in the eyeRinse with lots of clean running water for a long time, holding the eye open. Get medical help and take the product label.
Chemical on skinRemove contaminated clothing (with gloves) and wash skin with plenty of water.
Suspected broken boneKeep the limb still in the position found; support it with padding. Do not try to straighten it.
SprainsRest, cold pack wrapped in a cloth, support, and raise the limb.
Heat exhaustionMove to shade, loosen clothes, give sips of water if conscious, cool with wet cloths. Get help if confused or not sweating.
Snake biteKeep the person calm and still, remove rings and watches, keep the limb still and get to hospital fast. Do not cut, suck or put ice on the bite.

Never do this

  • Do not give food or drink to an unconscious person.
  • Do not move a person with a possible spine injury unless there is danger.
  • Do not give medicines unless you are trained and allowed to.

Write down what happened and what you did, and give it to the paramedics and your supervisor.

Key points

  • Make sure the scene is safe before you help.
  • Use DRSABC; start CPR if the person is not breathing normally.
  • Press hard on severe bleeding and keep pressing.
  • Cool burns with running water for at least 20 minutes.
  • Hands-on training with an accredited provider is required before you act as a first aider.

quiz.question: What is the first thing to check at an emergency scene?
How deep should chest compressions be for an adult?
How long should you cool a burn under running water?

options.text: Until the person says stop, at most 10 seconds

quiz.question: Where do you place your hands for adult CPR?

options.text: In the centre of the chest

quiz.question: Blood soaks through the dressing on a wound. What should you do?

options.text: Put another dressing on top and keep pressing
Remove the dressing and start again

quiz.question: Ice and butter are good treatments for burns.
An unconscious person who is breathing normally should be placed in the recovery position.
What should you do for a snake bite? (select all that apply)

options.text: Cut the bite and suck out the venom
Keep the person calm and still
